title: Content-context native card with a video sub-asset carrying inline VAST

source.name: IAB Native 1.2 §6.2 — Content Context, Video Response
source.notes: All source records are retained in assets/sources.json by reference.sourceIds.

modifications: All auction, bid, creative, site and publisher identifiers are synthetic.
All domains use reserved .test names; no real user IDs, IP addresses, consent strings or tracker endpoints.
All text and SVG artwork are original; no public creative copied — only the field composition (a video sub-asset alongside title/icon/main/sponsor/desc) is adapted from the source example.
The vasttag payload is an original minimal, well-formed VAST 3.0 Inline document, not copied from any source.

Corrected the source example's plcmttype:11 to plcmttype:2, as required by the actual §7.3 enumeration (max defined value 4); the example contains a stale/invalid value — same class of correction as bn-native-25-social-wrapped's §6.1 fix.
device.ip is the documentation-only address 192.0.2.11; OS values describe a synthetic test device.
provenance.sanitized: Only synthetic identifiers, original fixture creatives, reserved domains and TEST-NET addresses. No live tokens, subscriber IDs or real tracking URLs.

pairApplicability.note: Every response bid references an offered impression/item; auction identifiers match.

specNotes: Protocol validity is based on cited fields, not on current Core output. Optional-field warnings do not make this pair invalid.

IAB Native 1.2 §4.5/§5.6 Video (Request/Response): a video sub-asset carries VAST markup in `vasttag`. Asset id 81 is requested as a `video` kind and returned as a `video` kind — nativeAssetKind matches, so no kind-mismatch finding is expected.

crosscheck.js's nativeAssetFitness has no video-specific fitness rule (no duration/mimes/VAST-well-formedness check against a native video sub-asset) — this is a documented absent capability (crosscheck map §6/§8 item 9), not asserted here as a defect because the spec does not mandate a specific finding id for it; the well-formed vasttag is simply accepted as present.

The top-level bid.adm is the native JSON envelope, not VAST XML itself — isVastShape(bid.adm) is false, so no rules-vast.js findings are expected on this response at all; the VAST document is opaque payload nested inside the native asset string.

renderNativeToHtml (public/ortbtools.app.js:3163) only inspects title/img/data sub-assets — a video sub-asset contributes nothing to the rendered synthetic card. Documented via expect.preview.capabilityGap, not asserted as a knownGap (no spec-mandated finding is missing; this is a rendering completeness note).
Browser assertions are proposed observables; this corpus has not been run in a browser for this case.
Do not infer rendering from analysis.status or iframe existence alone.

HTTPS Native image URLs use reserved .test domains and are not registered in tests/corpus/assets/manifest.json (assetRefs is empty) — the browser's img-src CSP blocks any remote fetch regardless of interceptor/manifest registration, so no stored fixture is required for this pair's blocked/partial assertions; do not permit live DNS/HTTP traffic.

Current production preview CSP blocks remote Native images. Record card-text rendering and image blocking separately; intercepting a request does not bypass CSP. Do not claim fully rendered images if naturalWidth remains zero.
Inspect intended click target without following it.
notes: Core observations in the source archive were deliberately excluded from expectations. Protocol metadata may describe a vendor-specific 2.x carrier; it does not claim a normative minor-version inference.
